data.title: Nasdaq rebounds but posts fourth straight weekly decline
data.description:
Technology stocks bounced back on Friday from their worst drubbing in more than a year, but the Nasdaq Composite Index ​posted a fourth consecutive weekly decline as investors sifted for clues about what comes next in the AI trade.

Gains within technology ‌were broadly shared, with the semiconductor index rallying 4.2%. Nvidia rose 2.8%, Advanced Micro Devices added 11% and Sandisk rebounded almost 4%. Shares within the sector opened strongly and held much of their gains, with the Nasdaq ending up 1.1% after trading as much as 2% higher.

The broad revival underscores investor faith in the AI buildout that has driven US ​stock indexes to dozens of record closes this year, despite a shakeout that began with a US long-term Treasury yield spike in August ​and the stock volatility of the past month.

“We still think AI is the dominant theme in this bull market,” ⁠said Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services in Atlanta. “We are still giving technology the benefit of the doubt.”

The S&P 500 climbed 23 ​points, or 0.32%, to end the session at 7,376.86 points. The Nasdaq gained 264 points to 24,579.43 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 237 points, ​or 0.46%, to 51,285.73 points.

Lerner said he views the selloff this week, which has taken the Nasdaq into correction territory denoting a 10% decline from its peak a month ago, as likely offering a longer-term buying opportunity for many investors. For the week, the Nasdaq declined 3.4%, the S&P dropped 2.7% and the Dow slipped 0.9%.

“AI has gone on ​trial several times in this cycle and come away with an innocent verdict,” said Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist for LPL Financial in Charlotte, North ​Carolina. Referring to the US midterm election results that spurred heavy selling in AI stocks, he said, “This week we saw a little bit of a knee-jerk reaction.”

The S&P 500 ‌sectors were ⁠mixed, with information technology leading gains and consumer staples and healthcare lagging. The benchmark index had its worst week in more than a year.

US nonfarm payrolls increased more than expected in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, suggesting the labor market remained resilient. Traders added to bets that the Federal Reserve could hike rates as soon as next month, with a 78% chance of a December move compared with a 70% chance seen earlier, according to LSEG.

"Those are ​strong numbers,” said Joe Saluzzi, co-head ​of equity trading at Themis Trading ⁠in Chatham, New Jersey. But he asked, “Will the Fed want to raise interest rates in the face of a market which is teetering?"

Tesla rose 4.2% and SpaceX jumped 8.6% among technology shares bouncing back from Thursday’s plunge. Among other ​stock movers, software firm Atlassian dropped 16% after reporting first-quarter results. Airbnb climbed 12% after the vacation rental ​platform raised its full-year ⁠2026 revenue growth forecast.

Oil prices were slightly lower, adding to bullish sentiment for riskier assets, and were on track for sharp weekly declines. The S&P 500 energy index dropped 12% for the week, its worst performance since April 2025.

Despite the volatility, Turnquist said a bullish sign for the AI buildout is the performance of copper, ⁠a major ​ingredient in data centers and other technology. Copper futures remain above their 200-day moving average ​and their September lows, he said.

“If this is real demand destruction on AI, you’d think copper would start to roll over,” Turnquist said. “It’s not a perfect barometer, but I look at it as ​a reality check.”

data.title: Trump administration ends California balloting lawsuit
data.description:
The Trump administration on Friday withdrew its lawsuit that attempted to block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters whom federal officials alleged were likely non-US citizens.

  • The Justice Department filed a notice of voluntary dismissal in the case after the midterm elections that saw Democrats win by comfortable margins in all of California's statewide contests and most of its congressional races

  • On Monday, the day before the election, the Supreme Court rejected a bid to temporarily block California from counting the ballots on the Justice Department's list

  • The Justice Department had argued in previous filings that it needed quick action from federal courts because the contested ballots could not be separated from all other votes once they were accepted. The department again pointed to that reasoning in Friday's notice of dismissal, writing that "the relief the United States sought is no longer available" now that votes have been tallied

  • US District Judge David Carter had appeared skeptical of the Justice Department's lawsuit, expressing concerns that the request could disenfranchise and confuse legitimate voters, calling it a "monumental change" to election procedures when voting was already underway

data.title: Bitcoin Slips Toward 50-Week Moving Average, Putting Post-September Recovery To The Test: Weekly Close Streak Hangs In Balance
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bitcoin was trading at roughly $76,000, just 0.6% above its 50-week moving average.
  • Bitcoin has returned to the 50-week average in September for the first time since November 2025.
  • Alex Thorn at Galaxy noted that in four out of five completed bear markets the first break of the 50-week average marked the bottom.

Bitcoin (BTC) slipped to the brink of its 50-week moving average on Friday, threatening a run of weekly closes above the key trend line.

The apex cryptocurrency traded at around $76,000, leaving it 0.6% above its 50-week simple moving average (SMA) of $75,580. The 50-week SMA is the average closing price of Bitcoin over the past 50 weeks, or around a year, and is typically viewed by traders as an indicator of the long-term trend.

The slide began on Thursday when Bitcoin posted its biggest single-day loss since June, falling 5.5% from about $80,100 to $75,700. The selloff continued on Thursday, with the price hitting a low of $74,720. That briefly put it about 1.1% below average. Bitcoin recovered by the end of the session and closed back above the line at $75,800.

A Hard-Won Trend Line

Bitcoin has only just moved back above the average. It finished the week of September 20 at $81,150, Cointelegraph reported, citing TradingView data. At the time, the 50-week moving average was around $78,780. It was Bitcoin's first weekly close above the line since November 9, 2025.

Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy, has been closely following the level. In a research note in August, he had said the 50-week average had served as a ceiling in past bear markets. In four out of the five bear markets that have ended, the first break above the bottom was the bottom.

Galaxy also warned that the signal was not foolproof. Of 13 weekly crosses back above the average in past bear markets, two were followed by a lower low, both during the 2021-2022 downturn.

Bitcoin closed above the line for seven weeks in a row as of the close of the week ended Nov. 1. That close was $78,220, or 3.3% above the average, according to Galaxy. Since then, the cushion has shrunk to well below 1%.

At the time of writing, Bitcoin’s price was trading at $75,990, flat over the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, accompanied by ‘normal’ chatter levels over the past day.

Short-Term Momentum Fades

Bitcoin was down about 5.5% from its 10-week simple moving average of $80,522, according to data from Koyfin. The 10-week line moved above the 50-week line in October but was starting to flatten. The 50-week average was still heading lower, and it was down from over $100,000 at the start of the year, according to Koyfin.

The next test comes at the weekly close on Nov. 8, and a finish above the 50-week line would make it eight weeks straight.

A break below it would be the first one since the September reclaim and could revive fears of a false breakout.

data.title: Noel N. Tata to retire as Titan Vice-Chairman on November 12 upon turning 70
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Noel N. Tata will retire as Director and Vice-Chairman of Titan Company Limited on November 12, 2026, upon attaining the age of 70 years, in accordance with the Tata Group Governance Guidelines, the company said in an exchange filing.

In an exchange disclosure dated November 5, Titan said Tata would retire from the office of Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director and Vice-Chairman with effect from November 12.

The retirement is in line with the Tata Group's governance guidelines, which prescribe 70 years as the retirement age for Non-Executive, Non-Independent Directors.

Tata, who was appointed to Titan's board in March 2022, has been associated with the Tata Group for over four decades and holds leadership positions across several group companies.

He currently serves as Chairman of Trent Limited, Voltas Limited and Tata Investment Corporation Limited, while also holding the position of Vice-Chairman at Tata Steel. He is also Chairman of Tata International Limited and serves as Chairman of Tata Trusts.

The development raises questions about whether the age-based retirement provision will lead to changes in his board positions across other Tata Group companies.

However, Titan's November 5 filing only announces his retirement from its own board and does not indicate any decision regarding his positions in other group companies.

As per publicly available company disclosures, Tata was listed as Vice-Chairman of Tata Steel and Chairman of Trent, Voltas and Tata Investment Corporation in the respective corporate records and board profiles reviewed for this report. No corresponding retirement announcement from these companies has been established through the filings reviewed.

The cessation from Titan's board will take effect on November 12, the company said.
